Fixed bodies and an unrestricted base tilt give the exact argument shift for all finite real t. The ramp corners are null at positive width. Differentiating the covariance normalizer gives k = D·(w−Y) − (uᵀΣv)N·(w−Y), with a uniform O(h) argument remainder for bounded t. Only a slab of volume O(h) sees that remainder, so the scaled integrated error is O(h).

On the limiting plane m=−b, the test is D·(w−Y+b(0,Σu)), with the stated sign and no independently varying offset. The moving-column volume element after dividing by h is dr dξ/||u_l||. A proper section gives the complete line integral zero. An outside upper roof gives the integral from −∞ to q and an inside lower roof the complementary integral, hence opposite signs.

Dominated convergence off tangential relative boundaries, compact inner patch exhaustion and Hausdorff convergence handle all support types. The joint weak limit acts on all continuous bounded q and tangential tests, so the same subsequence works for every finite t and D. Infinite offsets contribute zero.

Integrated the piecewise-affine scalar residual independently in exact rational arithmetic over 425 pairs (q,s). Verified the lower and upper integrals, the two bounds on B and the saturated selector maximum, then checked the central coefficients at both corners, at an interior offset and off the ramp. The central symmetric coefficient is 1 on the open ramp, 1/2 at its two corners and zero away from the closed ramp, multiplied by k². In the corner-free record this recovers precisely the accepted χ covariance inequality.
